entries.title: AI Engineering Intern – Incident-Triage Agent
entries.summary: Ten-person student team building an AI agent that triages production alerts for Trafikverket's operations teams.
responsibilities: Designing an agent that reads the metrics, logs and source code behind an alert and proposes a diagnosis with next steps, so on-call engineers start from a hypothesis instead of a blank page.
Building it on self-hosted LLMs (Gemma) with a tool-calling agent loop, so no operational data leaves the organisation's network.
Integrating with Grafana, Prometheus and Kubernetes through a Python backend.

entries.title: Machine Learning Engineer – Sensor Classification
entries.summary: Classifying building and energy sensor types from metadata and time-series measurements.
responsibilities: Mapped PostgreSQL tables of sensors, devices, locations and measurement history and standardised inconsistent names, categories, units, labels, thresholds and multipliers.

Analysed more than 7.5 million time-series records from about 130 sensors for missing values, anomalies, value ranges, sampling frequencies and data gaps, and documented the workflow in Jupyter notebooks and Markdown reports.

entries.title: Full-Stack Developer – Access-Control System
entries.context: Client project via BTH, student team
entries.summary: Student team delivering an access-control system for shared Windows computers to Ericsson's requirements.
responsibilities: Built the Flask administration platform (SQLAlchemy, REST-style routes) for users, access schedules, account expiry, temporary access codes and login history.
Implemented schedule-based authorisation that checks account status, expiry, weekday and permitted time windows before granting access.
Connected the platform and Microsoft SQL Server to a C# Windows Forms lock-screen application handling card-based login, session control and audit logging.
